wstep: This card describes the NCHFP recipe for zucchini-pineapple: zucchini cooked in canned pineapple juice with bottled lemon juice and sugar, hot packed and processed in a boiling-water bath. [T:ACI-259,ACI-261,ACI-262]

sekcje.naglowek: Why you must not change the recipe
akapity: Zucchini is a low-acid food with a pH above 4.6. [T:ACI-026]
The FDA list gives cooked zucchini a pH of about 5.69–6.10. [T:ACI-086]
The whole product must contain a minimum, uniform level of acid so that botulism bacteria cannot grow. [T:ACI-017]
JarAtlas rule (cautious): do not change the amounts of bottled lemon juice, pineapple juice or zucchini; the recipe is tested only in the proportions given. [T:ACI-265]
NCHFP uses US measures: a cup holds about 237 ml. [T:ACI-195]

For about 8 to 9 pint jars NCHFP lists 4 quarts (about 3.8 l) of cubed or shredded zucchini, 46 ounces of canned unsweetened pineapple juice, 1 1/2 cups of bottled lemon juice and 3 cups of sugar. [T:ACI-259]
JarAtlas counts the 46 ounces of juice as US fluid ounces, about 1.36 l; this is the larger of the two possible readings, so it means more acidic juice, not less. [T:ACI-260]
Peel the zucchini and either cut it into 1/2-inch (about 1.3 cm) cubes or shred it. [T:ACI-261]
Mix the zucchini with the other ingredients in a large saucepan and bring to a boil. [T:ACI-261]
Simmer for 20 minutes. [T:ACI-261]
Fill the jars with the hot mixture and cooking liquid, leaving 1/2 inch (about 1.3 cm) of headspace. [T:ACI-261]
Put on the lids and process. [T:ACI-261]
At 0–1000 ft (up to 300 m) process half-pint and pint jars in a boiling-water bath for 15 minutes. [T:ACI-262,ACI-176]
Above 1000 ft the food may spoil if the time is not increased. [T:ACI-015]
At 1001–6000 ft (above 300 m up to 1800 m) process them for 20 minutes. [T:ACI-263,ACI-176]
Above 6000 ft (above 1800 m) process them for 25 minutes. [T:ACI-264,ACI-176]
The card converts feet to metres and rounds the limits down, towards the longer time: 1000 ft becomes 300 m and 6000 ft becomes 1800 m. [T:ACI-176]
Shortening the time or cooling jars in cold water can also lead to spoilage. [T:ACI-015]
The NCHFP table gives times only for half-pint and pint jars. [T:ACI-262]
JarAtlas rule (NCHFP does not test metric jars): a pint holds about 473 ml, so a 0.5 l jar has no tested time in this recipe; use jars of up to 473 ml. [T:ACI-179,ACI-174]
